key_insight: A standardized, multi-dimensional benchmark (AFIB) reveals that current LLMs show uneven financial intelligence: they can generate plausible analyses but struggle on factual accuracy, recency, consistency, and systematic failure modes.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a systematic, multi-faceted evaluation framework for assessing LLM capabilities in financial analysis and investment research.
method: Introduce AFIB: a benchmark assessing five dimensions—factual accuracy, analytical completeness, data recency, model consistency, and failure patterns.
Apply AFIB to multiple LLM-based financial AI systems (five engines evaluated) using curated financial prompts, time-sensitive data tests, and error-pattern analysis.
Quantify performance per dimension and identify common failure modes to guide model selection, fine-tuning, and risk mitigation.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and financial teams a practical rubric to compare models, prioritize robustness improvements, and make informed deployment choices for investment workflows.
visual_elements: Radar chart comparing models across the five AFIB dimensions (accuracy, completeness, recency, consistency, failures).
Stacked bar or heatmap of common failure patterns (e.g., hallucinations, stale-data errors, inconsistent reasoning) by model.
Timeline/recency test diagram showing model performance drop-off as data becomes older.
Simple evaluation pipeline diagram: prompts → AFIB tests per dimension → aggregated scores + failure analysis.
paper_title: Evaluating Financial Intelligence in Large Language Models: Benchmarking SuperInvesting AI with LLM Engines
paper_authors: Akshay Gulati, Kanha Singhania, Tushar Banga, Parth Arora, Anshul Verma
